stories.title: EggLab: Local AI image generation and editing for Windows - a design agent for PhotoCraft powered by Qwen-Image-2.1 (no ComfyUI, no Python, no cloud)
stories.body:
Local AI image generation and editing for Windows. A floating egg opens a design agent for PhotoCraft — chat, generate, edit layers, and place results straight onto the canvas.

Everything runs on your own GPU: Qwen-Image-2.1 on stable-diffusion.cpp. No ComfyUI, no Python, no cloud rendering. What it can do • Chat with a design agent that knows PhotoCraft: layers, masks, text, exports. • Generate images (quality 40-step or turbo 8-step LoRA) at up to 2048 px. • Edit images — reference photos, multi-reference compositions, transparent cut-outs. • Place results on the PhotoCraft canvas as layers, or export flat/layered files. • Local-first — models and renders stay on your disk; only chat text goes to the model provider you pick.

stories.title: rounds: A local canvas of everything your Claude Code sessions make
stories.body:
I run a lot of Claude Code sessions at once and kept losing track of what each one made. Now it all lands in one place, and I can leave notes on it. Try it

The demo is six of my public projects and the real notes I left on them. It runs in its own folder and doesn't touch your setup. What it does

Screens, pages and pushes from every session, sorted by project.

stories.title: Quoting Levent Alpöge
stories.body:
I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I …

I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too. Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions.

stories.title: Shrine of the Most Blessed Sacrement in Hanceville, Alabama
stories.body:
Roman Catholic church and monastery with extraordinary architecture designed to resemble a 13th-century Italian Franciscan church, particularly the Basilica of Saint Francis of Assisi.

Extraordinary architecture designed to resemble a 13th-century Italian Franciscan church, particularly the Basilica of Saint Francis of Assisi. Marble floors, gold ornamentation, stained glass, and soaring ceilings. The Spanish religious-art workshop Talleres de Arte Granda, founded in Madrid in 1891, designed and furnished the church's interior. It was founded by Mother Angelica, the founder of EWTN, and opened in 1999. Three donors provided all of the funds needed for construction and completion.
